hook: A Safe-class entry about a vast machine far beneath Site-19 that is really a radio drama: a researcher on the surface, and a D-class plus his stricken handler deep underground. Most of the page is dialogue, and the classified document titles slotted between the logs are worth reading as part of the story. Expect strong language and a death.
whyItMatters: The description is kept to a bare setup and the logs do all the work. The Supplemental Documentation blocks show nothing but titles and clearance levels, yet read in sequence they form a second, silent storyline running alongside the conversation. Two of those titles are Ethics Committee minutes.
thingsToNotice: The first switch sends lightning into DeWalt and leaves him paralysed, one tunnel goes dark, and the door they entered by turns out to be shut. Koullette keeps Charles going with deep breaths, Colorado's blue sky and a promise he will see it again, while the document titles move from re-entry attempts to the compromise of Sublevels 36-38, an anomaly mobilization directive and finally a Site-19 evacuation. The dark tunnel grows berries and fills with bats that settle and stare at him; DeWalt keeps gazing into it until his gaze looks relaxed, the water ran out early, Charles snaps that DeWalt would not have made it anyway, and his last log describes himself alone with a corpse. Told he will be left there until he presses the emergency button, Charles guesses it shuts off the power, heat and lights, and because he is afraid of the dark he decides to leave the lights on.
